label: CAUSE_OF_BEING_2: sustaining cause of being, giving a thing being at every moment it is present
definition: SustainsBeing h G v c x: x is present at some moment of history v, and at every moment t at which x is present, c gives x being at t (BeingGiving.GivesAt v c x t). Ordinary meaning: a cause whose activity goes on as long as its effect is. Examples: the sun lighting the air, which 'does not continue to be lit up, even for a moment, when the sun ceases to act upon it' (q.104 a.1 co.); as a model of the time profile only, a hand holding a stone aloft (what is sustained there is the stone's being held, not the stone's being). Counterexamples: the builder of a house, whose house stands after building stops (on either reading; q.104 a.1 co. makes him a cause of the house's becoming, not of its being); the fire that heated water that stays hot for a while after (q.104 a.1 obj. 2 and co.). Distinguished from CAUSE_OF_BEING_1 (originating), from preventing corruption (q.104 a.1 ad 3), and from repeated annihilation and recreation (q.104 a.1 ad 4; Feser 2021 rejects this reading of conservation). Meant on the strict, esse-giving reading of GivesAt. It types the concurrence of the activity with the effect, not the effect's dependence on it.
note: Analyst reading, attribution deferred: a time-indexed image of direct per se conservation of esse (definition 56989bd0, sourced to q.104 a.1 co. and ad 4, which has no Lean declaration). Not identified with it: 56989bd0 describes an action without motion or time on which the creature depends; this definition types only that the action bears on the creature at every moment at which it is present. OPEN: the dependence clause. Structural properties: none built in; not transitive by definition; mutual sustaining is not excluded by the type. Rival: existential inertia (Schmid 2021) denies that persisting things need any sustaining cause; it is compatible with every caused thing having an originating cause.
